title: Active Continual Learning with Metaplastic Binary Bayesian Neural Networks
topic: General Machine Learning->Online Learning, Active Learning and Bandits
claim: The next state is shaped jointly by the current loss (plasticity), the previous state (stability), and the prior (forgetting).
layout: Hub-and-spoke: three inputs with labeled arrows converging on a central output network
description: A hub-and-spoke schematic. Three small network diagrams sit at the top-left, top-right and bottom-center. Each has an input node, three hidden nodes and an output node, with arrows between them. Paired bars on every edge show Bernoulli probabilities for -1 (dark red) and +1 (dark blue). The top-left network is the previous posterior, q(ω|λ_{t-1}), labeled Stability. The top-right network is the prior p(ω), labeled Forgetting. Its bars are nearly equal, so it is close to uniform. At the top center, the loss L(λ_{t-1}, D_t) is labeled Plasticity, with a thick black arrow pointing down. Thick horizontal arrows from the left and right point to the central term q(ω|λ_t). The bottom network, the updated posterior, has bars that blend the three influences. The large black labels and the red and blue bars draw the eye first.
caption: Schematic of the BiMU update. The next variational state is shaped jointly by the current loss (plasticity), the previous posterior (stability), and the prior (forgetting). Bars show Bernoulli probabilities for ω ∈{−1, +1}.
abstract: Always-on edge systems must keep learning as conditions change under tight compute budgets and must detect unreliable predictions. Bayesian binary neural networks are attractive in this setting, but mean-field Bernoulli posteriors can saturate on long non-stationary streams, wiping out epistemic uncertainty and freezing plasticity. We propose BiMU, derived from a bounded-memory variational objective that balances stability, plasticity, and forgetting. BiMU combines a data term with controlled relaxation toward the prior and an uncertainty-dependent step size that prevents saturation and sustains informative uncertainty. This non-degenerate posterior enables fully online, buffer-free active querying via Monte Carlo disagreement, reducing label queries and backpropagation updates under imbalance. BiMU sustains learning and strong OOD detection on 1000-tasks Permuted-MNIST, and on OpenLORIS-Object achieves up to 32$\times$ label/update savings at matched accuracy under class imbalance and feature compression.
